## Class 7 sql
```{r}
con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "../data/scout.db")
postings = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "scout_postings") |> tibble::as_tibble()
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)  ##setting up for sql

jobs = postings |> 
  dplyr::select(company, location_state, remote, posted_at, last_seen_at) |>
  dplyr::filter(remote == 1) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    posted_at = as.Date(posted_at),  #changing data types
    last_seen_at = as.Date(last_seen_at),
    days_open = as.numeric(last_seen_at - posted_at)
    )

con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "../data/scout.db")
postings = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "scout_postings") |> tibble::as_tibble()
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)

jobs = postings |>
  dplyr::select(company, title, location_state, remote, category, posted_at, last_seen_at) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::ends_with("_at"), as.Date),
                days_open = as.numeric(last_seen_at - posted_at))

jobs

# Q1 -- which cat is remote friendly
# To answer that, the logic would be as follows"
# - Find the number of jobs per category
# - Normalize the number of remote jobs by dividing by the total jobs


jobs |> 
  # I want to move from unit of analysis being a job posting to a category
  dplyr::group_by(category) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    postings = dplyr::n(),
    remote_share = mean(remote)
  )

# Among full-time postings, which states have the highest remote share
# Based on the vote in class, I will deviate from the answer in the slide 
# by showing the combination of category and state -- this will still give you the answer you want

jobs |> 
  dplyr::group_by(category, location_state) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    postings = dplyr::n(),
    remote_share = mean(remote) |> round(digits = 2)
  ) |> 
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(remote_share)) |> 
  na.omit() # to drop the location_state == NA and any other rows that contain NA

# Notes logic
jobs |> 
  dplyr::filter(category == 'fulltime') |> 
  dplyr::group_by(location_state) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    postings = dplyr::n(),
    remote_share = mean(remote) |> round(digits = 2)
  ) |> 
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(remote_share)) |> 
  na.omit()
```

#airbnb

```{r}
con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "../data/midwest_airbnb.db")
listings = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "listings") |>
  tibble::as_tibble()
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
dplyr::glimpse(listings)

# 1. How many listings per city?
## If the answer is purely based on last class, I can group by city and then count the number of listing in each city

listings |> dplyr::group_by(city) |>   dplyr::summarise(count = dplyr::n())
# alternatively, the short cut for the code above
listings |> dplyr::count(city) # count does group by and then n()
# the other option is to simply count the number of times each city occurred in the col city
table(listings$city) # returns a named vector vs above we get a data.frame/tibble

# 2. For entire homes (room_type == "Entire home/apt") that sleep four or more, what is the median price in each city?
listings |> 
  dplyr::filter(
    room_type == "Entire home/apt" & accommodates >= 4
  ) |> 
  dplyr::group_by(city) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    median_price = median(price)
  ) -> q2
q2

#  Q3: Add price_per_person = price / accommodates. Which three listings are cheapest per person? Believe them?

listings |> 
  dplyr::mutate(price_per_person = price / accommodates) |> 
  # for the sake of printing nicely, I will reduce the number of cols
  dplyr::select(city, host_name, name, price, accommodates, price_per_person) |> 
  dplyr::arrange(price_per_person) |> 
  head(3)

# Which five host_names have the most listings? [FYI -- host names are not unique]
# host_ids are

listings |> dplyr::count(host_name, sort = T)

# the line below groups by both host_name and host_id (to attempt to find unique hosts) -- this is the gist of the question but both answers would have been considered correct on an exam given the way I framed the question
listings |> dplyr::count(host_name, host_id, sort = T)
```

# example

```{r web scraping}
# checking whether we are allowed to scrape this info
# This was done above and found to be TRUE

# I will load the backend of the HTML into R using
# [a] rvest::read_html() | sometimes rvest::read_html_live() if the page has some dynamic content
# [b] in some cases, we will craft this as a request as shown in slides httr2::request() > .... > httr2::resp_body_html()
isa_courses_in_r = rvest::read_html("https://bulletin.miamioh.edu/courses-instruction/isa/")

# we will extract the course titles, which we can do in a single pipeline
# given that they look the same on the rendered web page in Chrome
# (bolded, same font size and same font type)

# CSS selector was obtained by:
# [a] highlighting what we wanted to pull (ISA 401 course title) in Chrome -> right click
#  inspect -> right click > copy -> copy selector
# [b] from this specific example, we were able to get just the title for ISA 401
# because we had `:nth-child(24)` -> if you were to drop it --> you get all the course titles
isa_courses_in_r |> 
  rvest::html_elements("#sc_sccoursedescs > div > p.courseblocktitle > strong") |> 
  rvest::html_text2() -> isa_titles
  
# course descriptions [using selector gadget, which does not always work]
# but when it works it is easier

isa_courses_in_r |> 
  rvest::html_elements(".courseblockdesc") |> 
  rvest::html_text2() -> isa_desc

df = data.frame(title = isa_titles, description = isa_desc)
```

## class 11 scraping multiple pages

```{r bulletin}
dept_abbrv = c('acc', 'bus', 'isa', 'mkt')
#use for loop
courses_df = data.frame() # initializing a container to store stuff in from the loop
for (abbrv in dept_abbrv) {
  cat( rep("-", 50) , "\n" )
  print(abbrv)
  bulletin_url = paste0(
    'https://bulletin.miamioh.edu/courses-instruction/', abbrv, '/'
  )
  
  # Q: Why did Fadel make this an R object instead of a string like last class?
  # [a] we did this so we can reuse the rest of our code with only changing the URL
  webpage = rvest::read_html(bulletin_url)
  
  webpage |> rvest::html_elements("strong") |> rvest::html_text2() -> titles
  webpage |> rvest::html_elements("p.courseblockdesc") |> rvest::html_text2() -> descs
  
  df = data.frame(title = titles, desc = descs)
  print(df$title[1:2])
  courses_df = rbind(courses_df, df)
}


```

```{r purrr}
dept_abbrv = c('acc', 'bus', 'isa', 'mkt')

# This function takes an abbrv as an input and returns a data_frame as an output
scrape_mu_bulletin = function(abbrv){
  bulletin_url = paste0(
    'https://bulletin.miamioh.edu/courses-instruction/', abbrv, '/'
  )
  
  # Q: Why did Fadel make this an R object instead of a string like last class?
  # [a] we did this so we can reuse the rest of our code with only changing the URL
  webpage = rvest::read_html(bulletin_url)
  
  webpage |> rvest::html_elements("p.courseblocktitle") |> rvest::html_text2() -> titles
  webpage |> rvest::html_elements("p.courseblockdesc") |> rvest::html_text2() -> descs
  
  df = data.frame(title = titles, desc = descs)
  return(df)
}

test = scrape_mu_bulletin(abbrv = 'eco')

# to use functions from purrr, we will use a map_*(), or map2_*(), or a pmap_*()
# map uses a function that takes a single input (or you are only changing a single input)
# map2 uses a function that takes two inputs
# pmap >=3
# after the _, you put the type of object you are getting back

# the .x is the vector that we will iterate over
# and the .f is the function we use

courses_df_from_purrr = purrr::map_df(.x = dept_abbrv, .f = scrape_mu_bulletin)
```


```{r game}
page = rvest::read_html("https://isa401-salvage.vercel.app/registry?start=1")
classes = page |>

sum(Dreadnoughts_df$value)

```

## Class 13 Tidying and Having Technically Correct Data from the PlaneCrash Info Site

```{r crashes}
year = 2025

crash_url = paste0('https://www.planecrashinfo.com/', year, '/', year, '.htm')

# the encoding came from chatisa as shown in class 12
crash_page <- rvest::read_html(crash_url, encoding = "ISO-8859-1")

crash_page |> 
  # selector from inspector (kept the last three parts of the selector)
  # note the output (we also dropped :nth-child(8) in tr since we want all rows)
  rvest::html_elements("tr > td:nth-child(1) > font") |> 
  rvest::html_text2() -> date_col

crash_page |> 
  # repeat for location_operator
  rvest::html_elements("tr > td:nth-child(2) > font") |> 
  rvest::html_text2() -> location_operator

crash_page |> 
  # repeat for aircraft_reg
  rvest::html_elements("tr > td:nth-child(3) > font") |> 
  rvest::html_text2() -> aircraft_reg

crash_page |> 
  # repeat for fatalities
  rvest::html_elements("tr > td:nth-child(4) > font") |> 
  rvest::html_text2() -> fatalities

# note that the number elements in the four vectors are not equal
df = data.frame(
  date_col = date_col, 
  # -1 drops the first row that had the col header
  location_operator = location_operator[-1],
  aircraft_reg = aircraft_reg[-1],
  fatalities = fatalities[-1]
)

# make this tidy

df |> 
  tidyr::separate(col = location_operator, into = c("location", "operator"), sep = "\n") |> 
  tidyr::separate(col = aircraft_reg, into = c("aircraft", "registeration"), sep = "\n") |> 
  tidyr::separate(col = fatalities, into = c("air_fatalities", "num_pass", "ground_fatalities")) -> tidy_df
```

```{r complex API Request}
toxic_ips = readr::read_csv("../data/toxic_ips_oct2025.csv")

ip_addresses = toxic_ips$IP

x = ip_addresses[1]

ip_api = function(x){
  paste0(
    "http://ip-api.com/json/", x,
    "?fields=status,message,continent,country,countryCode,region,regionName,city,district,zip,lat,lon,timezone,currency,isp,org,as,query") |> 
    jsonlite::fromJSON() -> response
  
  response |> as.data.frame() -> df
  
  return(df)
}

ip_df = purrr::map_df(.x = ip_addresses, .f = ip_api)

ip_df |> tibble::tibble() # so it prints better
```

```{r}
library(rvest)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)

# Read the HTML page
page <- rvest::read_html("https://realpython.github.io/fake-jobs/")

# 1. Extract each element one at a time using corrected CSS selectors
title <- page |> 
  rvest::html_elements("div.card-content h2.title") |> 
  rvest::html_text2()

company <- page |> 
  rvest::html_elements("div.card-content h3.company") |> 
  rvest::html_text2()

location <- page |> 
  rvest::html_elements("div.card-content p.location") |> 
  rvest::html_text2()

date_posted <- page |> 
  rvest::html_elements("div.card-content time") |> 
  rvest::html_text2()

apply_link <- page |> 
  rvest::html_elements("footer.card-footer a:nth-child(2)") |> 
  rvest::html_attr("href")

# Combine the individual 100-length vectors into a data frame
fake_jobs_df <- tibble(
  title = title,
  company = company,
  location = location,
  date_posted = date_posted,
  apply_link = apply_link
)

# 2. Count job titles containing "Python"
python_jobs_count <- sum(stringr::str_detect(title, stringr::regex("Python", ignore_case = TRUE)))

# View output
dplyr::glimpse(fake_jobs_df)
print(python_jobs_count)
```
